titleStmt.title: Sørge- og Klage-Sange over den nu i Døden høysalige Konge, Kong Friderich den Femte

work.title: Sørge- og Klage-Sange over den nu i Døden høysalige Konge, Kong Friderich den Femte

history.p: There is no indication in the printed text book, which is the only surviving source, as to whom author and composer were. However, in some of the sections the text is identical to the mourning cantata performed at The Musical Society commemorating the death of Queen Louise in 1752 (SchW B2:430). At that event the poet was Gerhard Schaft and the composer and leader of the performance was Scheibe. It seems highly likely that the music to the present cantata performed at The Musical Society was the same but the text was revised in accordance with the present event, that is commemorating the death of Frederik V in 1766. According to one of the newspapers, Kiøbenhavns Adresse-Contoirs Efterretninger, the Society issued a selection of mourning songs (‘Sørge- og Klage-Sange’) performed by characters such as 'Rumour', 'Fortune', 'Virtue' and 'Patience' which agree with those of the present printed libretto. The rehearsal was on 14 March but the newspaper does not indicate when the concert was to take place.

incipText.p: Rinder I Taarer, og ikke aflader!
Ey noget Tordenslag kan os saa bange giøre
Der er fornummet en Røst i det Høye
Hvad nu! hvad Graad! hvad Jammer-Skrig!
Hvad har dig Dyd bekymret giort?
See Femte Fridrich med Dyder var prydet
See! Fred paakom en Bitterhed, ja en Bitterhed
Nu sidde vi da og begræde

annot.p: No indication of character but perhaps 'Taalmodighed' who sings the following section.

incipText.p: Vel er den følesløs, ja, har et Tiger-Hierte
Om Dig skal hver en Tunge

annot.p: No indication of character, but if the recitative is sung by 'Taalmodighed', it seems likely that this aria was also performed by 'Taalmodighed'.

incipText.p: Hvad Trøst kan vel Opmuntre vores Siel?
Du Kongers Konge giv vor Konge Fryd og Glæde!
